Results.ReviewText:
We bought this at the end of the fall grilling season in 2018.  Wow. We were impressed with the high quality aluminum grill casing and the even cooking temperature. The grill gets hot very quickly.  Plenty of upsides plus a great warranty. 
However, with that said. This grill is very light in weight and with no bottom door to keep strong winds out, be wary about a strong wind gust picking the grill up and sending it flying off the patio.  This could have been a disaster if we were using the grill or if children or frail adults were nearby. For that matter, anybody getting hit by a hot grill would be a disaster. We love the grill. We are disappointed with the lack of wind protection. 

Now again for the good news. After I put the grill back together, there was no damage that I could tell and the LP gas line connection has two lines that are linked with a L shaped bracket. One line connects to the tank and the line was still attached to the tank. The other line was still attached to the grill venturies.  

Be careful with this product. Happy grilling!
Results.Title: Great Weber Grill product, but.....

Results.ReviewText: We’ve enjoyed Weber grills for over 20 years until we purchased this one in 2018. The tray below the burners that catches all the marinade and food particles and it doesn’t fall to the tiny tray below so the grill goes on fire often and had to be taken apart and cleaned. The tiny tray that slides out gets caught all the time and it doesn’t hold a disposable tray very well. The food doesn’t burn off inside the large box like tray and there’s always an odor.  This grill is lighter than most of the other Weber grills and blows over when it’s windy. All of the knobs busted off when it fell over. The Weber cover that fits this grill doesn’t fit well. The Velcro spots don’t fasten well and the cover constantly blows off. Here’s the real catch why I hate this grill so much. When it’s uncovered and it rains, the grill leaks. Water seeps into the large tray draining all the guck inside the grill onto our patio cement so I’m always freaked about keeping the grill clean inside and covered. Do not buy this grill

I followed the instructions to turn the grill on and leave it to set the grate. I then cooked some burgers which immediately stuck!!
So despite Weber’s claims that these new grates need no special curing, I ended up curing the grate by piling and leaving at high temperature for 20 minutes after which I cooked burgers again, this time perfectly. 
It’s disappointing. I also have a 12 year old all stainless Genesis which still works perfectly. 
Weber- if the design works please stop trying to fix it!!

Results.ReviewText:
I bought this grill about four months ago to replace the Weber gas grill I had used hard for 20+ years.  THAT was a great grill.  This is a fantastic grill!  It actually has more usable flat surface for putting things down, yet has a slightly smaller footprint than its predecessor.  Added bonus:  One of those surfaces folds down against one side of the grill, which decreases the space it takes up when "at rest".

This grill is more sturdy as well.  I was skeptical about the use of plastics in the base, but it really does seem more rugged, nearly indestructible, because of that material.  It's also lighter.  I loved my old grill, so I can't believe I'm saying this:  The burner system is a big improvement over the older design.  I didn't think I would like the front-to-back design, but now I love it.  It also gives much more flexibility for things like indirect heat.  The old one, about the same overall dimensions, just had two long burners running side-to-side.

The control knobs seem more sturdy as well.  Everything about this grill just screams high quality.  Gotta love what Weber has done to improve their product line over the years.

I'm not planning to use the wireless access features, but it's cool that it's ready for that.  Overall I have to say that this is a wonderful grill, well worth what I paid for it, and I'm glad I stuck with the Weber brand.

Results.ReviewText:
I had a high end Weber for about 15 years before it completely fell apart.  Their high end is so expensive that I dabbled in cheaper no-name brands, but they rarely lasted for more than 2-3 years and were always difficult to cook on, with various hot and cold spots.  
The Spirit II is an excellent grill for the money.  It has very even heating, easy maintenance, and an excellent size.  I also know I can get replacement parts in the future and should be able to keep this grill for a decade or more.
